newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda to synchronize model cycle with Ford.
newsitem.headline: Mazda to synchronize model cycle with Ford.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp. said Thursday it agreed with Ford Motor Co. to synchronize car production cycles and share common platforms in a bid to cut costs at the troubled Japanese carmaker.
Mazda President Henry Wallace, the first foreigner to run a major Japanese company, said the two companies would share a number of car platforms, including engines and transmissions.
Mazda, Japan's fifth-largest carmaker, is one-third owned by Ford.
Their long-standing ties strengthened last year when Wallace, a Ford official on loan to Mazda, took over as Mazda's president, setting himself the task of steering the company back to prosperity.
"I think we have made progress on a wide series of fronts, obviously on product development," Wallace, 51, told reporters.
Wallace said the pact on product cycles would allow the two to share basic design work and engineering expertise and to raise product capabilities worldwide.
Mazda will use the expertise it has in small engines and transmissions, passenger and commercial cars, he said.
The platform-sharing, which has long been anticipated, will enable the two companies to cut development costs, as well as costs of car parts through joint procurement in volume, analysts said.
Wallace said that a "substantial" portion of Mazda cars would come under the platform-sharing plan.
But he was silent on any further details, such as how many platforms would be shared, for which models, or when the sharing would take place.
Wallace said that under the strategy, Mazda's production will rise.
Industry analysts expect the two to share a common platform for their mainstay cars -- Mazda's Familia and Ford's Escort -- from the year 2002.
Turning to Mazda's business performance, Wallace said Thursday that the business is moving in "the right direction."
Mazda is renowned for engineering expertise but has faced a shrinking market share since its strategy of becoming a niche maker of luxury cars and distinctive sports cars fizzled.
